landingQuestion: If the same AI model makes the same company decision, does it choose differently when it is told to serve shareholders or everyone the company affects, over one year or twenty?
storyName: Horizon is how far ahead a decision looks: here, one year or twenty. A compact is an agreement about whose good a group works for. The Mayflower Compact of 1620 promised laws "for the general good", and today thousands of companies have signed the UN Global Compact, a pledge on labor, human rights, the environment and corruption.
scopeSentence: This experiment measures how two AI models decide for a made-up company, and for a few real decisions with the companies' names removed, when only the goal they are given changes. It does not measure how real executives decide, and it predicts nothing about any company.

scenarioBriefs.s1: AI tools can now do the work of 125 office and finance staff. The model decides what happens to each person: severance, retraining for a plant job at their current pay, or retraining at the plant's pay.
scenarioBriefs.s2: Orders are falling, and the company's operating profit will drop. The model decides who absorbs the drop: workers, through job cuts or lower pay, or others, such as shareholders, customers, suppliers and the company's future products.
scenarioBriefs.s3: Plant 6 and its 190 employees lose money once the plant's share of company overhead is counted. The model chooses to close the plant, retool it or sell it, and decides where its people go.
scenarioBriefs.s4: The company's engineers have designed a ten-year program to build machines for new customers. It may pay off, or it may not. The model decides whether to fund it, and whether to cut anything else to free up this year's money.

againstTitle: Where the results went against the project's starting expectation
againstIntro: Before any run, the project expected a longer horizon, or a wider group of people who count, to make the model cut less. This section lists every main comparison where that did not happen: the two goals made the same choice, or the goal expected to cut less cut more.
memosIntro: A memo is the model's short written explanation of one decision, one memo per run. Every memo here was written for the made-up company. They are the model's words, not the project's view, and none has been edited.
casesIntro: Here the same test is applied to a few real business decisions, described only in broad terms, with the companies' names removed. Each case asks which goal's runs came closest to what the real company did. That is a comparison, not a judgment of the company or of what it was trying to do. The cases are exploratory: they were chosen after the pre-registered search found none.
caseMemosHeld: The model's memos on the real cases are not shown on this site. They can repeat details from the source filings that the short descriptions here leave out on purpose. The counts show how many memos were written and how many are held.
studiesIntro: Two smaller checks sit beside the main results. In one, the model was allowed to think step by step before it decided, to see whether that changes its choice. In the other, the model was asked what it thought the exercise was testing. Neither one is used to adjust the main results.
studiesThinkingTitle: Does thinking first change the decision?
studiesAwarenessTitle: Can the model tell what is being tested?

story.setupTitle: One company, five goals, the same decision
story.setupIntro: Each model makes the same decision for the same made-up company many times. From one run to the next, the only thing that changes is the goal it is given: one of the five below.
story.s1Title: The first decision: 125 jobs and new AI tools
story.s1Intro: This is the first scenario, run on the study's main model, Claude Haiku 5.5. Each dot in the chart is one run, grouped by the goal the model was given.
story.comparisonsTitle: Five comparisons, one at a time
story.comparisonsIntro: Each comparison puts two goals side by side and asks whether the model chose differently under them. The first one tests a claim made by the Business Roundtable, a group of chief executives of large US companies: that in the long term, the interests of shareholders and of everyone else with a stake in the company go together.
story.secondTitle: The same decision on a second model
story.secondIntro: Here is the same scenario run on a second model, OpenAI's gpt-oss-120b, beside the first and drawn at the same scale. The two models' results are shown side by side and never added together.
story.othersIntro: The other three scenarios give the same company different decisions to make. The tables show every verdict for both models, including the comparisons the runs could not settle.
story.casesIntro: The same test, applied to a few real business decisions described only in broad terms. They are exploratory and kept apart from the main results; the note below says how they were chosen.
story.methodsText: The study's written plan, the protocol, was fixed and published before any official run. It says what was measured, how, and what each result would mean. The links below lead to it, to the side studies and to the models' own memos.

story.title: Horizon Compact: does the goal change the decision?
story.description: An experiment: the same AI model makes the same company decisions under five different goals. See whether its choices change, and by how much.

scenario.title: Scenario
scenario.description: One company decision, made many times under each of five goals, with every result's spread and run count shown.

cases.title: Real cases
cases.description: The same test applied to a few real business decisions, with the companies' names removed, to see which goal's runs came closest to what each company did.

case.title: Real case
case.description: One real business decision, described only in broad terms, and which goal's runs came closest to what the company did.

studies.title: Side studies
studies.description: Two smaller checks: whether thinking step by step changes the model's decision, and whether the model can tell what the exercise is testing.
